name: Susan Wojcicki
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Rented garage to Google founders in 1998 (~30) and joined as Google employee #16 / first marketing manager in 1999 (~31); YouTube CEO 2014–2023 (~45–54).
early_history_summary: Born July 5, 1968 in Santa Clara County, California; daughter of Stanford physicist Stanley Wojcicki and educator Esther Wojcicki. Harvard history/literature A.B. (1990), UC Santa Cruz M.S. economics, UCLA MBA; early marketing roles at Intel, Bain, and R.B. Webber before Google.
family_context_summary: Father Stanley Wojcicki was a Stanford physics professor; mother Esther Wojcicki a well-known educator/journalist; sister Anne Wojcicki later founded 23andMe.
parent_family_domain_summary: Academic/educational elite family with Stanford proximity; not tech-operating founders themselves.
evidence_summary: Career breakout milestones (Google garage 1998, hire 1999, AdWords leadership, YouTube CEO) all occurred well after age 26. Elite education and family academic status are clear but do not substitute for a dated ≤26 material milestone.

name: Meg Whitman
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Princeton economics, Harvard MBA (1979, ~23), then brand manager at Procter & Gamble; eBay president/CEO from 1998 (~42).
early_history_summary: Born August 4, 1956 on Long Island, New York; Princeton B.A. economics and Harvard MBA 1979. Early corporate marketing/consulting path (P&G, Bain, Disney, Hasbro) before joining eBay as CEO when it had ~30 employees.
family_context_summary: Raised in affluent Cold Spring Harbor / Oyster Bay area of Long Island; detailed parental occupations not emphasized in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as tech/e-commerce domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Standard elite post-MBA career entry at P&G at ~23 is not coded as a material trajectory-defining milestone. Defining achievement was scaling eBay (1998–2008) in her early 40s, followed by HP/HPE leadership.

name: Jack Ma
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. At ~26 (1990) still an English teacher in Hangzhou after 1988 graduation; China Pages ~1995 (~31); co-founded Alibaba in 1999 (~35).
early_history_summary: Born Ma Yun September 10, 1964 in Hangzhou; struggled with gaokao, graduated Hangzhou Normal University 1988, taught English, then entered internet entrepreneurship in the mid/late 1990s leading to Alibaba.
family_context_summary: Described as ordinary/modest Hangzhou family background in multiple profiles; not a privileged capital family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources as business/tech domain expertise.
evidence_summary: Alibaba founding (1999) and China Pages (~1995) both after age 26. Teaching English and early job rejections in his 20s do not constitute material entrepreneurial milestones under the rubric.

name: Ma Huateng
milestone_by_age_26: No material ≤26 milestone found. Co-founded Tencent in November 1998 at age 27 (born Oct 29, 1971); prior R&D role at China Motion Telecom after Shenzhen University CS (1993).
early_history_summary: Born October 29, 1971 in Guangdong (Shantou/Chaoyang area); CS degree Shenzhen University 1993; worked on internet paging systems at China Motion Telecom before cofounding Tencent with classmates including Zhang Zhidong in 1998.
family_context_summary: Limited family wealth detail in English sources; grew up partly in Shenzhen tech environment.
evidence_summary: Tencent founding date is 1998; SCMP and other sources explicitly place him at age 27. Strict age≤26 rule excludes the founding as the qualifying milestone; no earlier material founding/product breakout documented.

name: Lei Jun
milestone_by_age_26: No clear material breakout by age 26 found. Joined Kingsoft 1992 (~22); regional GM roles mid-1990s; Kingsoft CEO 1998 (~28–29); Xiaomi founded 2010 (~40).
early_history_summary: Born December 16, 1969 in Xiantao, Hubei; Wuhan University CS 1991; joined Kingsoft as early employee (often described as sixth), rose through product/leadership roles, led Kingsoft IPO 2007, then founded Xiaomi in 2010.
family_context_summary: Described as rural/schoolteacher-parent background in Hubei with limited connections; not affluent.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents described as schoolteachers in some profiles; not software-industry domain transfer.
evidence_summary: Early Kingsoft employment and internal promotions before 26 are career progression, not independently material public milestones. Defining milestones (Kingsoft CEO, IPO, Xiaomi founding) are all after age 26.

name: Robin Li
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. RankDex algorithm/site-scoring work dated 1996 (age 27–28); Baidu founded January 2000 (~31). At 26 (through Nov 1995) working at Dow Jones/IDD after Peking University and Buffalo MS.
early_history_summary: Born Li Yanhong November 17, 1968 in Yangquan, Shanxi to factory-worker parents; Peking University information management; University at Buffalo MS CS; Dow Jones/IDD engineer 1994–97; Infoseek 1997–99; co-founded Baidu with Eric Xu in 2000.
family_context_summary: Fourth of five children, only son of factory workers in Yangquan, Shanxi; ordinary industrial-family background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were factory workers; no documented search/tech domain transfer.
evidence_summary: RankDex (1996) and Baidu (2000) both after age 26. Strong technical work at Dow Jones/Infoseek in mid/late 20s is real but the dated material inventions and founding fall outside the ≤26 window under strict age math.

name: Niklas Zennström
milestone_by_age_26: No material founding milestone by age 26 found. Began at Tele2 ~1991 (~25) in telecom ops; co-founded KaZaA ~2000 (~34) and Skype 2003 (~37).
early_history_summary: Born February 16, 1966 in Järfälla, Sweden to teacher parents; Uppsala University business and engineering physics degrees; Tele2 career in the 1990s before partnering with Janus Friis on KaZaA and Skype.
family_context_summary: Parents were teachers in Sweden; middle-class professional household.
evidence_summary: Tele2 employment starting ~25 is ordinary corporate entry, not a material founder/product milestone. KaZaA and Skype—the career-defining ventures—came in his 30s.

name: Kevin Mitnick
milestone_by_age_26: By age 17 (1980–81), arrested for unauthorized access after social-engineering and breaching Pacific Bell COSMOS systems; already known for phone phreaking and computer intrusion that made him a lasting security-world figure long before his 1995 FBI capture.
early_history_summary: Born August 6, 1963 in Los Angeles; raised by mother after parents' divorce; phreaked buses/phones as a teen, obtained amateur radio license, broke into DEC and telecom systems in late teens/early 20s, leading to 1988 DEC-related conviction and later multi-year fugitive period.
family_context_summary: Born to Alan Mitnick and Shelly Jaffe in Los Angeles; Jewish family; parents divorced; raised largely by mother and maternal grandmother Reba Vartanian; not a wealthy tech family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as computer-security domain expertise; path was self-taught street/phone-phreak culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen phreaking, social engineering, Pacific Bell COSMOS, DEC intrusion, LA phone/computer underground
evidence_summary: Mitnick's ≤26 materiality is multi-sourced: first hacking arrest ~17 (Pacific Bell), sustained unauthorized access to major corporate/telecom systems through early 20s, and 1988 conviction for DEC-related software theft at ~24–25. He became a defining public face of 1980s–90s computer crime and later a top security consultant/author after prison. Advantage stack is almost entirely self-built skill and underground peer practice rather than family capital or elite institutions.
starting_point: Born 1963 in Los Angeles to a modest Jewish family; parents divorced; raised primarily by mother in the San Fernando Valley without elite tech capital.
current_position: Died July 16, 2023 at age 59 of pancreatic cancer; final roles included Mitnick Security Consulting founder and Chief Hacking Officer at KnowBe4.

trajectory.event: Arrested after Pacific Bell COSMOS intrusion and related computer/phone crimes, establishing national-level early notoriety.
Convicted in connection with unauthorized DEC network access and software copying; sentenced to prison plus supervised release.
Captured by FBI in Raleigh after multi-year fugitive period involving cloned cell phones and corporate network intrusions.
Pleaded guilty to wire fraud and computer fraud counts; sentenced to multi-year federal prison term.
Released from prison and began transition to legitimate security consulting and public speaking.
Published The Art of Deception; built Mitnick Security Consulting and later KnowBe4 advisory role as elite social-engineering expert.
Died of pancreatic cancer in Pittsburgh; remembered as the world's most famous reformed hacker-turned-security consultant.

name: Adrian Lamo
milestone_by_age_26: In 2001–2002 (ages ~20–21), publicly documented grey-hat intrusions into Yahoo!, Microsoft/Excite@Home, WorldCom, and The New York Times networks—national media coverage and a 2003 federal arrest/2004 felony guilty plea followed while still under 26.
early_history_summary: Born February 20, 1981 in Malden, Massachusetts to a Colombian father; high-school dropout with GED in San Francisco area; self-taught Commodore 64/phone-phreak path; transient 'homeless hacker' lifestyle while probing major corporate networks and notifying vendors.
primary_leverage_engine: Scarce technical depth / security research notoriety
family_context_summary: Father Mario Ricardo Lamo was Colombian; family details sparse; Lamo lived a highly independent, often unhoused lifestyle as a young adult.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as cybersecurity domain expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: homeless hacker lifestyle, grey-hat disclosure, NYT/Microsoft/Yahoo intrusions, early web security era
evidence_summary: Lamo's ≤26 milestone is independently verified: SecurityFocus/Wired/CNET covered his 2001–2002 high-profile network compromises, WorldCom praised fixes, NYT filed complaint, and he surrendered/ pleaded guilty in 2003–2004 at ages 22–23. Later (2010) he reported Chelsea Manning to authorities, a second major public act after 26. Early advantage is self-taught skill plus platform-era media amplification, not family capital.
starting_point: Born 1981 in Massachusetts to a Colombian father; raised partly in California; left high school without diploma and adopted a transient independent lifestyle.
current_position: Died March 14, 2018 in Wichita, Kansas at age 37; cause of death never definitively established; final public identity as threat analyst known for the Manning case.

trajectory.event: Publicly exposed security flaws at Excite@Home/Yahoo!-class networks as a grey-hat researcher, drawing national security press.
Breached The New York Times internal systems and LexisNexis access; WorldCom publicly credited him for security help.
Surrendered to federal authorities after multi-month investigation; became a leading face of early-2000s ethical/grey-hat hacking debates.
Pleaded guilty to felony computer crimes; sentenced to probation, home detention, and $65,000 restitution.
Reported U.S. Army analyst Chelsea Manning to authorities over WikiLeaks document leaks, becoming a polarizing public figure.
Died in Wichita; forensic review found no definitive cause of death.

name: Kim Dotcom
milestone_by_age_26: Arrested in 1994 (~20) for trafficking stolen phone calling-card numbers and, in 1998 (~24), convicted in Germany on 11 counts of computer fraud and 10 of data espionage—establishing him as a high-profile European hacker-entrepreneur well before Megaupload.
early_history_summary: Born Kim Schmitz January 21, 1974 in Kiel, West Germany (Finnish mother); teen hacker alias Kimble claiming high-profile breaches; ran piracy BBS 'House of Coolness'; later stock-trading/Kimvestor persona and, after 26, Megaupload (2005) and New Zealand political activism.
family_context_summary: German father, Finnish mother from Turku; holds Finnish passport; not described as inherited-wealth elite; early path was street-hacker not family firm.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech/business domain transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: teen Kimble hacking, phone-card fraud, 1998 German conviction, early internet entrepreneurship
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Wired, Fast Company, and German-case reporting corroborate 1994 arrest and 1998 multi-count computer-fraud/data-espionage conviction with suspended sentence while still under 26. Megaupload (2005, age ~31) and the 2012 New Zealand raid are later. Early edge was self-directed underground technical practice and internet-era arbitrage, not elite schooling or family capital.
starting_point: Born 1974 in Kiel to a German father and Finnish mother; limited formal education (Hauptschule); entered hacker/BBS culture as a teenager.
current_position: Living in New Zealand (recently Dunedin for medical care after a reported stroke); long-running U.S. extradition fight over Megaupload charges continues after 2024 extradition order.

trajectory.event: Arrested in Germany for selling stolen phone calling-card numbers; early national notoriety as hacker Kimble.
Convicted on 11 computer-fraud and 10 data-espionage counts; received a two-year suspended sentence described by the judge as youthful foolishness.
Executed high-profile Letsbuyit.com share trade that drew market and legal scrutiny in Europe.
Launched Megaupload, which grew into one of the world's largest file-hosting services by traffic.
Arrested in a large New Zealand police raid at U.S. request; Megaupload seized; multi-year extradition litigation began.
Launched Mega cloud storage successor and later the Internet Party in New Zealand politics.
New Zealand Minister of Justice signed extradition order to the United States; judicial review efforts continued.

name: Julian Assange
milestone_by_age_26: In December 1996 (age 25), pleaded guilty to 24 Australian computer-hacking charges stemming from International Subversives intrusions (including Nortel and broader military/industrial targets), receiving a fine and good-behaviour bond after a high-profile federal investigation—material early notoriety years before WikiLeaks.
early_history_summary: Born Julian Paul Hawkins July 3, 1971 in Townsville, Queensland; itinerant childhood across 30+ Australian towns; skilled teen hacker 'Mendax' from ~16; formed International Subversives with Trax and Prime Suspect; later cypherpunk/programming work and WikiLeaks (2006).
family_context_summary: Mother Christine Hawkins (visual artist); biological father John Shipton (anti-war activist/builder); raised largely by mother and stepfather Brett Assange (actor); highly mobile, often precarious childhood; not inherited wealth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Arts/activism household rather than computer-security profession; technical path was self-taught.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Mendax/International Subversives, Nortel hack, 1996 conviction, cypherpunks, Underground book research
evidence_summary: Assange's ≤26 milestone is the documented International Subversives hacking career culminating in 1994 charges and December 1996 guilty plea to 24 counts (Sydney Morning Herald, Guardian, Christian Science Monitor, Wikipedia multi-source). WikiLeaks founding (2006, age ~35) and Cablegate (2010) are later. Advantage stack is self-created technical depth, peer hacker group, early online communities, and adversity from unstable childhood—not elite capital or institutions.
starting_point: Born 1971 in Queensland; itinerant Australian childhood across dozens of towns with artist/activist parents and limited financial stability.
current_position: Living free in Australia after June 2024 U.S. plea deal (time served) ending UK detention and extradition fight; remains WikiLeaks publisher/figurehead.

trajectory.event: Active as skilled Australian hacker under handle Mendax, beginning multi-year International Subversives activity.
AFP Operation Weather raid after Nortel Melbourne terminal intrusion; major federal computer-crime case begins.
Pleaded guilty to 24 hacking-related charges; fined and bound over on good behaviour rather than imprisoned.
Co-founded WikiLeaks as anonymous-source publishing platform focused on organizational transparency.
Published Manning-sourced Collateral Murder video, Afghan/Iraq war logs, and U.S. diplomatic cables, becoming a global political figure.
Entered Ecuadorian embassy in London seeking asylum after Swedish extradition case and U.S. pressure.
Pleaded guilty in Saipan to one Espionage Act conspiracy count for time served; returned to Australia free.

name: Edward Snowden
milestone_by_age_26: No public material milestone by age 26 found. CIA technical hire ~2006 (~22–23) and Geneva posting ~2007 are early career jobs; defining global surveillance disclosures came in June 2013 at age 29–30.
early_history_summary: Born June 21, 1983 in Elizabeth City, NC; family of federal/Coast Guard public servants near Fort Meade; GED after mono interrupted high school; brief Army SF candidate 2004; security guard then CIA (2006–09) then Dell/NSA contractor path leading to 2013 leaks.
family_context_summary: Father Lonnie Coast Guard warrant officer; mother Elizabeth court clerk (Maryland federal court); sister lawyer; maternal grandfather Coast Guard rear admiral/FBI official—strong federal-service family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Federal government/military family near Fort Meade intelligence corridor; domain proximity to classified work is real but employment itself is not the ≤26 public milestone.
evidence_summary: CIA entry-level technical services work and Dell/NSA contracting before/around 26 are private-sector/government employment, not independently material public achievements. The world-changing act—leaking PRISM and mass-surveillance programs—occurred at age 29–30 in 2013.
